title: Layer stack, isometric

techniques.name: Layer stack

step.label: Step
step.note: The page’s four steps through the stack: say, count, keep, reach back. Each lights its plate and its leader.

gap.label: Layer gap
gap.note: How far the plates are drawn apart, as a share of a plate’s length. The page’s own is 72.5% (5.8 of 8 units); below 66% the tallest count block reaches the plate above. The drawing is refit to its frame.

axis.label: Axis angle
axis.note: The angle the plates’ edges make with the horizontal, set by how high the eye sits: 30° is isometric. Lower flattens the plates; higher opens them up toward a plan, up to where the blocks would reach the plate above.

po.label: Unlit plates
po.note: How strongly the plates off the current step show. The page’s own is 50%; at 100% every plate is lit alike and the step is marked only by its lime edge.

kw.label: Keyline
kw.note: Weight of the drawing’s object lines (plates, blocks, ticks, recall rings) in the page’s pixels; the plate edges and the lit edge keep their proportion. Leaders and the dimension stay hairline.

techniques.implementation: Planes and stairs are drawn in one-point or isometric projection with hard flat color. Drawn by the source page’s own code; each dial sets one of the page’s own controls or one of the numbers its drawing is built from.

techniques.name: Measured inks
techniques.implementation: solid ink pixels of each figure, read at full resolution, are clustered to five colors; a color is kept when it holds at least 4% of the ink.

techniques.name: Figure and ground
techniques.implementation: The ground is the most common border color of a figure; ink is every pixel more than 40 levels from it.

pass_order: read · points measured from the figure
